content.text:
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG (`scripts/auto_release.sh`
  via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main (gh-1522: the retired flow
  pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit per release). gh-1801: NO
  GitHub Release is created at tag-cut time (an asset-less create
  published an empty `latest` that broke `fa update`): the tag-run
  `binaries` job creates the release DRAFT-first via
  `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (curated CHANGELOG notes via
  `release_notes.sh` + a `release-draft-owner` marker), every leg attaches
  into it, and `release-provenance` publishes + flags `latest` ONLY after
  the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) is attached — `latest` never points at a
  release that cannot serve `fa update`. The git TAG is the single source
  of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`
  jobs (the release publishes at the provenance step). `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
  `package-lock.json`s, and `vendor/wasm_run/native/Cargo.lock`); a listed
  lockfile that is missing/untracked/gitignored fails the Static gates, and
  pod-sync (flutter-analyze + nightly build legs, after `pub get`) fails
  when a native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by pubspec.lock has no pod in the
  platform's `Podfile.lock` (the gh-1274 class), or its pod is pinned at a
  stale version vs the resolved plugin podspec's `s.version` (the
  flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew; the podspec is the comparison target,
  not the pubspec version — vendored/beta pods legitimately differ from the
  Dart package version). The inventory also enforces the gh-1303 path-pin
  sync: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` pins this repo as a path dependency, so
  its `flutter_agent_harness` pin must EXIST and equal the root
  `pubspec.yaml` version — a stale OR MISSING pin (e.g. a merge conflict
  resolved by dropping the entry) makes every
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` consumer red — the pins are
  `0.0.0-dev` on both sides and NEVER churn across releases (gh-1522: the
  tag is the version; the release flow mutates zero files), and the Static
  gate catches any other path to the drift at PR time. After ANY pubspec.yaml
  dependency change that adds/updates a darwin-native plugin: `cd
  flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update` and the same in `macos/`,
  commit both `Podfile.lock`s (CocoaPods runs fine on Linux for
  regeneration; the wasm_run `nm` step needs an llvm-nm shim + the
  XCFramework staged via `scripts/setup_vendor_ios.sh` or the upstream zip).
  Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested (`scripts/
  check_lockfiles_selftest.sh`, Static gates).
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)
  runs the `submit_for_review` lanes — pure pre-flight in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb` (plain-ruby tested) fails
  BEFORE any mutation; already-submitted versions are a green no-op;
  release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click
  (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it, E5). Grep-guards:
  `test/store_automation_guard_test.dart`.
- App Store content pipeline (no binary): store screenshots are COMMITTED
  goldens from `flutter_app/test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart` (frame +
  inline en/ru copy in `store_marketing_frame.dart`) at
  `flutter_app/test/goldens/store/{en,ru}/{ios,ipad,mac}/` — regenerate with
  `flutter test test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart --update-goldens`,
  then open every PNG. Store copy lives in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/metadata/{ios,macos}/{en-US,ru-RU}/` (the lanes strip
  name.txt/subtitle.txt — App Info is not editable post-release); release
  notes come from the latest `## […]` section of
  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
  app_store` / `fastlane mac app_store` in `flutter_app` (env gates
  `IOS_DEPLOY_METADATA`/`IOS_DEPLOY_SCREENSHOTS`/`MACOS_DEPLOY_*`; ASC API key
  env secrets) or the `store-metadata.yml` workflow (`ios_content`/

# gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-macos:
    name: Build macOS ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    # gh-1600 F-A: pin the ONE self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1) via its
    # unique registration label — the generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # list also matched the Linux self-hosted box's labels (same routing
    # bug that sent the build-mobile iOS jobs to Linux, gh-1600).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #239: TestFlight submit now waits for Apple processing (bounded,
    # default 90 min) + a ~1-min one-shot appearance probe AFTER the
    # build/notarize work (gh-1041: the blocking distribution wait moved to
    # the deferred store-appearance-check workflow) — the job ceiling must
    # cover the worst case, not just the build.
    timeout-minutes: 150
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch: [arm64, x86_64]
    permissions:
      contents: write

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # gh-1522: the bundle version rides the TAG (GITHUB_REF_NAME), not
          # the committed placeholder pubspec.
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          grep -qi "usage" <<<"$out" || { echo "fa --help did not print usage"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          fi
          ls -lh "$asset"

[scripts/assert_release_assets.sh#BE19]
1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# gh-1832: release required-assets gate + post-publish smoke.
3:#
4:# The single source of truth for the required set is the file next to this
5:# script: scripts/release_required_assets.txt (scope rationale lives in its
6:# header). Three modes:
7:#
8:#   assert_release_assets.sh <tag>
9:#       PUBLISH GATE (ci.yml release-provenance, before the signed-checksum
10:#       upload and the --draft=false --latest flip): every required asset
11:#       name must already be attached to <tag>'s release (draft counts).
12:#       Anything missing → ::error:: + exit 1 → the release run goes red
13:#       and the release stays a draft (the previous release stays latest).
14:#       This is the rehearsal-proven guard for the v1.0.635 incident, where
15:#       the extension's producer (build-macos.yml build-extension, a daily
16:#       leg that derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment") attached
17:#       fa-extension.zip to an orphaned v1.0.636 draft while the tag train
18:#       published v1.0.635 without it — every leg green, nothing asserted
19:#       the published set.
20:#
21:#   assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>
22:#       POST-PUBLISH SMOKE: ranged-GET (1 byte) every required asset's
23:#       download URL; anything outside HTTP 200/206 fails. Base URL is
24:#       https://github.com unless FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE overrides it
25:#       (tests), repo comes from GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
26:#
27:#   assert_release_assets.sh --landing [page]
28:#       LANDING LINK-CHECK: extracts EVERY http(s) …/releases/(latest/)?
29:#       download/… URL from the landing page (default site/index.html) and
30:#       probes each the same way — the page's links can never silently rot
31:#       again (the owner-facing symptom of gh-1832 was exactly this 404).
32:#
33:# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN (gate mode), FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE
34:# (smoke/landing override, tests only).
35:set -euo pipefail
36:
37:script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
38:required_file="$script_dir/release_required_assets.txt"
39:[ -s "$required_file" ] || {
40:  echo "::error::required-assets list $required_file is missing/empty — refusing to judge a release against an empty set" >&2
41:  exit 1
42:}
43:# The list, comments stripped, order kept.
44:required=()
45:while IFS= read -r line; do
46:  line="${line%%#*}"
47:  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
48:  [ -n "$line" ] && required+=("$line")
49:done < "$required_file"
50:[ "${#required[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
51:  echo "::error::$required_file parsed to zero assets — fix the list" >&2
52:  exit 1
53:}
54:
55:# One ranged GET; prints the HTTP code. 200/206 = served (206 = the
56:# Range: bytes=0-0 answer of a real CDN download, i.e. an actual
57:# 1-byte download probe, not a name check).
58:probe_url() {
59:  local url="$1" code
60:  code=$(curl -sS -L --range 0-0 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
61:    --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || true
62:  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
63:  # Always emit the code (the caller's success line shows it); the
64:  # function's exit status carries the verdict.
65:  echo "$code"
66:  case "$code" in
67:    200|206) return 0 ;;
68:    *) return 1 ;;
69:  esac
70:}
71:
72:mode="${1:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh <tag> | --smoke <tag|latest> | --landing [page]}"
73:
74:case "$mode" in
75:  --smoke)
76:    tag="${2:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>}"
77:    repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
78:    base="${FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE:-https://github.com}"
79:    fail=0
80:    for asset in "${required[@]}"; do
81:      if [ "$tag" = "latest" ]; then
82:        url="$base/$repo/releases/latest/download/$asset"
83:      else
84:        url="$base/$repo/releases/download/$tag/$asset"
85:      fi
86:      if ! code="$(probe_url "$url")"; then
87:        echo "::error::release asset smoke FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: a required asset does not serve)" >&2
88:        fail=1
89:      else
90:        echo "✅ $url → HTTP $code"
91:      fi
92:    done
93:    [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
94:    echo "✅ required-assets smoke passed for $tag (${#required[@]} assets)"
95:    ;;
96:
97:  --landing)
98:    page="${2:-site/index.html}"
99:    [ -f "$page" ] || {
100:      echo "::error::landing page $page not found — pass the path or run from the repo root" >&2
101:      exit 1
102:    }
103:    # URL stops at whitespace, quotes, angle/close parens, plus, comma —
104:    # the landing page embeds these links in hrefs and JSON FAQ text with
105:    # trailing punctuation. NOTE: grep -E cannot portably put a tab in a
106:    # bracket expression ('\t' there means backslash and letter t, which
107:    # would truncate every URL at its first 't') — build the class with a
108:    # real tab via printf.
109:    url_class="[^\"' <>()+,$(printf '\t')]"
110:    urls=$(grep -oE "https?://${url_class}+" "$page" \
111:      | grep -E '/releases/(latest/)?download/' | sort -u || true)
112:    [ -n "$urls" ] || {
113:      echo "::error::no /releases/ download links found in $page — the page shape changed; revisit the link-check contract (gh-1832)" >&2
114:      exit 1
115:    }
116:    count=0
117:    fail=0
118:    while IFS= read -r url; do
119:      count=$((count + 1))
120:      if ! code="$(probe_url "$url")"; then
121:        echo "::error::landing link FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: the landing page exposes a broken release download)" >&2
122:        fail=1
123:      else
124:        echo "✅ $url → HTTP $code"
125:      fi
126:    done <<< "$urls"
127:    [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
128:    echo "✅ landing link-check passed: $count release URL(s) in $page all serve"
129:    ;;
130:
131:  *)
132:    tag="$mode"
133:    repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
134:    export GH_TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
135:    [ -n "$GH_TOKEN" ] || {
136:      echo "::error::GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN is not set — the gate cannot read the release's asset list" >&2
137:      exit 1
138:    }
139:    on_release=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets \
140:      --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
141:    missing=()
142:    for asset in "${required[@]}"; do
143:      if ! printf '%s\n' "$on_release" | grep -qxF "$asset"; then
144:        missing+=("$asset")
145:      fi
146:    done
147:    if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
148:      echo "::error::release $tag is missing ${#missing[@]} required asset(s): ${missing[*]} — BLOCKING the publish (gh-1832: a partial release must never go live; the release stays a draft and the previous release stays latest). Producers: fa-extension.zip ← build-macos.yml build-extension (daily cli leg), fa-linux-*/fa-windows-* ← ci.yml binaries, fa-web-spa.zip ← ci.yml web-spa, fa-macos-* ← ci.yml binaries. Re-run the missing producer against this tag, then re-tag/re-run the train." >&2
149:      exit 1
150:    fi
151:    echo "✅ release $tag carries all ${#required[@]} required assets — publish may proceed"
152:    ;;
153:esac

💡 **SUGGESTION: `probe_url` has no retry and swallows curl's stderr**

`scripts/assert_release_assets.sh:60-61`:

```bash
code=$(curl -sS -L --range 0-0 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || true
```

Two small robustness gaps in the probe every post-publish signal depends on:

1. `2>/dev/null` discards the `-sS` error text, so a transport failure surfaces only as the opaque `HTTP 000` in the `::error::` line — the reason (DNS, TLS, redirect loop) is lost exactly when someone is triaging a red smoke job.
2. No `--retry`: one transient CDN 5xx or connection reset during the post-publish window reds the smoke and costs a human look even though the asset is fine. The gate mode is immune (name check, not HTTP), but the smoke runs once per train.

Suggested:

```bash
code=$(curl -sS -L --range 0-0 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 \
  --retry 2 --retry-all-errors "$url") || true
```

(keeping stderr visible or echoing `curl`'s error into the failure line). Non-blocking — the probe is fail-closed either way, and a red smoke can simply be re-run.
